title: APPROVAL OF FOREIGN-TRADE ZONE (FTZ) DEVELOPER AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT AND WATSON LAND COMPANY, FTZ 202, SITE NOS. 10 AND 11
text:
RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVAL OF FOREIGN-TRADE ZONE (FTZ) DEVELOPER AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT AND WATSON LAND COMPANY, FTZ 202, SITE NOS. 10 AND 11

Transmittal 2
Transmittal 3
Summary
: Staff requests approval of a Foreign-Trade Zone (FTZ) Developer Agreement (Agreement) between the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department) and Watson Land Company (Watson Land), to continue to maintain their FTZ status and promote the FTZ Program within FTZ 202, Site Nos. 10 and 11, located in Carson, California. Watson Land is a real estate investment firm whose principal address is in Carson, California. Site Nos. 10 and 11 consist of 325.5 acres of warehouse and 153.79 acres of office space. The property is located approximately 9 miles north of the Port of Los Angeles. The proposed action is aligned directly with the Harbor Department’s Strategic Plan, Objective 3: Improved Financial Performance of Port Assets, Initiative 2: Increase the utilization of Port facilities and develop a plan to activate vacant port properties. FTZs are specifically designed to stimulate economic activity, utilize port property, and generate revenue. Approving developer and operator agreements directly activates port properties and designated zones, bringing in businesses that utilize the Port's ecosystem. The proposed action also aligns with the Harbor Department’s Strategic Plan, Objective 2: An Efficient, Secure, and Sustainable Supply Chain, Initiative 1: Facilitate supply chain efficiencies and terminal velocity with stakeholders, with continuous enhancements to the Port Optimizer product. FTZs provide distinct operational and regulatory advantages that streamline how cargo moves through the logistics chain. They allow cargo operators to defer, reduce, or eliminate customs duties. This financial and administrative incentive attracts cargo volumes, reduces customs clearance delays, and improves overall supply chain velocity for Port stakeholders. The proposed Agreement is for a term of five years with three, five-year renewal options. Watson Land has had a Developer Agreement since 2020, however, it expired in April, 2025.
Recommendation
: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article II, Section 2(f) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) approve the proposed Foreign-Trade Zone Developer Agreement between the Harbor Department and Watson Land; 3) authorize the Executive Director to execute and the Board Secretary to attest to the proposed Foreign-Trade Zone Developer Agreement; and 4) adopt Resolution No. _________.
